title: What snapshots can and cannot tell
learning_goal: Know the Rice estimator's bias and variance and its test conditions, the threshold bound on reversal rates, why waiting times need dynamics, and what the next round of tier 0 must show.

sentences.text: How wide should Rice's strip be?
Widen it: the estimate blurs, its bias growing like the width squared.
Narrow it: the estimate jitters, as fewer snapshots land inside.
The three-dial experiment used snapshots within zero point two of zero.
With endless snapshots, why not shrink it to nothing?
The exact formula assumes a smooth cloud. A cosine has only a thin ring, yet the formula still finds two crossings per period.
Chaos may lack a smooth cloud too, so nothing guarantees the limit: on the three dials, the only test so far, the answer depends on the strip.

onscreen.title: Rice's formula, as an estimator
labels: What snapshots can and cannot tell
snapshots on a thin ring: no smooth density
deterministic chaos: smooth density not guaranteed
only test so far: three deterministic dials

formulas.tex: \ck{\hat r_0}(h) = \frac{1}{2hN}\sum_{i=1}^{N} |\dot D_i|\,\mathbf 1_{|D_i|<h},\qquad \mathbb E\big[\ck{\hat r_0}(h)\big] = \ck{r_0} + \frac{G''(0)}{6}\,h^2 + o(h^2),\quad G(d) = \int |\dot d|\,p(d,\dot d)\,d\dot d

\mathrm{Var}\big(\ck{\hat r_0}(h)\big) = \frac{M(0)}{2Nh} + O\!\left(\tfrac{1}{N}\right)\ \ (N\ \text{independent snapshots}),\quad M(d) = \int \dot d^{\,2} p(d,\dot d)\,d\dot d;\ \ h^\star \propto N^{-1/5},\ \text{error}^2 \propto N^{-4/5}
\text{deterministic chaos: the physical measure can be singular (Young 2002), so } (D, \dot D) \text{ may have no density; E1 keeps } h = 0.2\ (\text{R:528, R:901})

chips: illustration · synthetic Gaussian snapshots, true rate known · no data
error bars assume independent snapshots: generated ones are, one simulation's are not · T:691
needs F: the speedometer comes from the equations
tested on a 3-variable deterministic system only

sentences.text: To count reversals, not crossings, raise the bar: a reversal must run from above some level to below its mirror image.
So the level's {metric}crossing rate{/}, which Rice reads from snapshots, caps the reversal rate.
Wobbles across the level loosen the cap.
The conjecture: if a flip lasts far longer than a wobble, the cap is nearly exact on a plateau of levels.
The bet, from the PhD plan: on the staircase's first step, the cap comes within thirty percent of the counted rate on that plateau.
Confidence: medium; the cap is proved, the plateau is not.
Ask first: how wide must that plateau be?

labels: a reversal: from above a to below −a
r_a · crossings of the level a, either way (Rice: snapshots + equations)
SCHEMATIC · the conjecture's picture, no data
Rice at level a · true snapshots

formulas.tex: \text{reversal } {+}\!\to\!{-}:\ D \ge a\ \text{then}\ D \le -a;\quad r_{+\to-} \le \tfrac12\,\ck{r_{-a}},\ \ r_{-\to+} \le \tfrac12\,\ck{r_{a}}\ \Rightarrow\ r \le \ck{r_a}\ \ (\text{law symmetric under } B \to -B),\quad \ck{r_a} = \mathbb E_\mu\big[|\dot D|\,\delta(D - a)\big]\quad \text{Prop. 2.30}

\text{Conjecture 2.33: reversal duration} \gg \text{turbulent correlation time} \ \Rightarrow\ \text{a range of levels } a \text{ with } r/\ck{r_a} \approx 1,\ \text{read off the curve } a \mapsto \ck{r_a}\ \text{(plateau)}
\text{tier 0, criterion (d): bound of Prop. 2.30 satisfied and tight within } 30\,\%\ \text{on a plateau of thresholds (T:889); metrics: } \ck{r_0}, \ck{r_a} \text{ against exact count (T:888)}

sentences.text: One more limit, a proved one.
These two smooth random signals share one snapshot law, value and speed alike: same Rice rate.
Yet one crosses zero like a metronome, the other at uneven gaps.
On three dials, Gissinger found a shape in the waits between flips: a comb of short, quantized waits, then a memoryless exponential tail.
No shoebox holds that shape; it takes the movie.
The open question: can short runs, launched from generated states in the corridor, supply the waits?

\text{waiting times need dynamics: integrate the true system, or a temporal emulator, from generated states; states near } |D| \approx 0 \text{ are the most informative (T:719); open question (T:131)}

question.en: Beyond *how often*: for VKS, should we also target *waiting times*, with short solver runs from generated states?
question.say: Beyond how often: for VKS, should we also target waiting times, with short solver runs from generated states?
question.fr: Au-delà de la fréquence : pour VKS, faut-il aussi viser les *temps d'attente*, avec de courtes simulations lancées depuis des états générés ?
question.why: Snapshots plus the equations fix how often the dipole crosses zero, never how long it waits (Prop. 2.32): waits need dynamics. Tier 0 already plans them cheaply (T:888); for VKS they cost solver time, and MilaDy's objective (i) is about reversal dynamics, precursor to recovery.
question.unblocks: Runs: whether the VKS tier budgets short SFEMaNS or LATU runs started from generated states in the corridor (how many, how long), and whether such states are valid starts. Framing: waiting-time laws as a criterion, or left to a temporal model.
question.why_fr: Les instantanés et les équations fixent la fréquence des passages par zéro du dipôle, jamais la durée de l'attente (proposition 2.32) : l'attente demande la dynamique. Le palier 0 la prévoit déjà à faible coût (T:888) ; pour VKS elle coûte du temps de solveur, et l'objectif (i) de MilaDy porte sur la dynamique des renversements, du précurseur à la récupération.
question.unblocks_fr: Simulations : le palier VKS prévoit-il de courtes simulations SFEMaNS ou LATU lancées depuis des états générés dans le couloir (combien, quelle durée), et ces états sont-ils des départs valides ? Cadrage : les lois des temps d'attente comme critère, ou laissées à un modèle temporel.
